DHI rebuild resets stale gzwrite input pointers before gzprintf/gzvprintf use the internal buffer, mitigating the out-of-bounds write class described for zlib 1.3.1.x in CVE-2026-85091. See https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-85091 and https://gist.github.com/thesmartshadow/e0b9481792afb7c31e86fee1ff084490.
Upstream patch ba829a458576d1ff0f26fc7230c6de816d1f6a77 applied. Adds negative length checks in crc32_combine64 and crc32_combine_gen64 to prevent CPU consumption from infinite loops.
Marked no-dsa by Debian Security Team; see https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-27171

False positive. CVE-2026-22184 affects the untgz utility that is part of zlib source code, but Debian zlib packages (zlib1g and zlib1g-dev) do not ship the untgz utility by default. For Debian Trixie (and other versions), zlib comes from zlib1g (binaries) and does not include the untgz binary. The vulnerability scanner incorrectly flags zlib packages as vulnerable when the untgz utility is not actually present in the installed packages.
